text:
G2 is a gap in the package. No spec, check, prompt or skill defines a findings document for a review unit. The package has no numbered findings with a file, a line and a blocking mark, and no check that refuses an incomplete one. I did not read how checks are registered in `checks.py` beyond its imports. The final line has the full account.

ARTIFACT gap_finding: No file in `plugins/temperspec-tgraph` defines a review findings document (numbered findings, each with file, line and blocking mark) or a check that refuses an incomplete finding. The triage row `docs/tasks/i173.triage.md` line 35 holds. Grep of `workflow/temperspec/checks.py` for "finding|blocking|numbered" finds only the engine's `CheckFinding` type (lines 15, 30-34), which is a check's own result record and not a review finding, and "blocking" only as a conversation value (line 695-699). Specs: "finding" appears only as check findings (`code.spec.md` ts-code-mixed line 30, `discovery.spec.md` ts-dis-over line 13, `judge-reading.spec.md` JRD-B7 lines 53-57, `kept-marks.spec.md`) and as reading-session findings lines (`parallel-reading.spec.md` PRL-B9 line 66, PRL-B11 line 80, PRL-B12 line 89, line 97: one line of at most 1,500 characters, claims to confirm). None has a file, a line or a blocking mark. `skills/review/SKILL.md` is the nearest wording and is a person's own skill, not a workflow step: findings lines 18-43, verdict `holds`/`does not hold`, each finding marked `must fix` or `worth fixing`, with file and lines, read-only. It is not numbered, has no check, and no step loads it. Models for the new check: `checks.py` `_find`/`_ok` (30-34); `ts-tri-form` refuses a triage note with "no numbered acceptance criterion" (line 655); `_owner` (694) refuses incomplete owner-decision entries, which is a form check on a note, and `specfmt.py` holds the formats the checks read. A new findings format would need `specfmt.py` parsing, a check, and a spec with criterion ids.
